title: Strong 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes eastern Indonesia
text: Strong earthquake hits Indonesia Indonesia Strong 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes eastern Indonesia Shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground after initial tsunami warning Guardian staff and agencies Fri 14 Aug 2026 19.43 EDT Last modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 21.32 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A powerful 7.7-magnitude quake struck eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the US Geological Survey said, sending thousands running in panic after authorities issued a tsunami warning. The shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region with a depth of 10km at 5.58am local time and was followed by two aftershocks, including one with a magnitude of 6.1. Residents in Nagekeo regency, the area closest to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated – a possible sign of an approaching tsunami. Authorities have since lifted the warning and no immediate casualties have been reported. “Suddenly it started to shake and I panicked,” 31-year-old hospital customer service official, Lukas Lotar told AFP. “Patients also fled the hospital, the jolt was big. I saw some walls were cracked,” he added. View image in fullscreen

title: Croatia denied visas to nine Russian gymnasts, then admitted four. One of them, Angelina Melnikova, later won gold.
text: Russian gymnast Angelina Melnikova won the individual all-around title at the 2026 European Championships in artistic gymnastics, held in Croatia, scoring 55.932 points. Russian gymnast Anna Kalmykova took second place with 54.632 points, and French gymnast Elena Colas placed third with 53.966 points. The competitors performed on the uneven bars, balance beam, vault, and floor exercise. The win made Melnikova a five-time European champion in artistic gymnastics and gave her the first individual all-around title of her career. She had previously won gold in the team event in 2016 and 2018, on the floor exercise in 2017, and on the uneven bars in 2021. Melnikova is also an Olympic champion — she won gold in the team event in 2020 — and a three-time world champion. This is the first time in five years that Russian gymnasts are competing at the European Championships, doing so under neutral status. The women’s European Championships in artistic gymnastics run in Zagreb from August 13 to 16, with the men’s tournament following from August 19 to 23. Authorities had issued a tsunami warning, which has since been lifted, but there have been dozens of aftershocks, including one with a magnitude of 6.1. Tsunami waves of ⁠less than one metre (three feet) were recorded in several areas. Indonesian geophysics agency BMKG recorded the first quake at 4.58 am local time at a depth of 15 ⁠km (9 miles) in Indonesia’s Flores region. Rescuers around the port town of Maumere found 20 dead, six injured and two trapped under the rubble, said Fathur Rahman, head of the city’s rescue agency. text: Фейк: Комар-убийца поселился в России и охотится на людей Правда: Численность комаров Anopheles plumbeus не достигает высоких показателей в России. Особенности данного вида в том, что личинки насекомого обитают в труднодоступных местах для человека. Активное обсуждение комара как переносчика тропической малярии началось после исследования ученых Государственного университета просвещения: они зафиксировали распространение этого вида на территории России. Однако Anopheles plumbeus впервые был выявлен в нашей стране в 1930-х годах. Да, этот комар действительно может переносить малярию, но его эпидемиологическое значение в РФ оценивается как невысокое. Это кровососущее встречается в единичных случаях, а его личинки живут в глубоких дуплах деревьев — это значительно ограничивает контакт человека с насекомым. Публикации основаны на искаженном исследовании, для привлечения большего внимания аудитории к материалам. title: Civilian Casualties in Ukraine in July Hit Highest Monthly Toll Since March 2022, UN Says
text: Civilian Casualties in Ukraine in July Hit Highest Monthly Toll Since March 2022, UN Says Aug. 14, 2026 Ukrainian State Emergency Service Civilian casualties in Ukraine in July reached their highest level since the early months of Russia's full-scale invasion, as Russian forces intensified long-range missile and drone strikes on towns and cities far from the front line, the UN said in a report published Friday. The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine confirmed that at least 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured last month, the highest toll in any month since March 2022. The figures represent a 30% jump from June and a 70% increase compared to July 2025. Long-range weapons, including cruise and ballistic missiles and drones, remained the primary cause of civilian casualties, accounting for 38% of all deaths and injuries in July. The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine confirmed that at least 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured last month, the highest toll in any month since March 2022. The figures represent a 30% jump from June and a 70% increase compared to July 2025. Long-range weapons, including cruise and ballistic missiles and drones, remained the primary cause of civilian casualties, accounting for 38% of all deaths and injuries in July. title: Yabloko Appeals Russian Supreme Court Ruling Barring It From State Duma Elections
text: Yabloko Appeals Russian Supreme Court Ruling Barring It From State Duma Elections Aug. 14, 2026 Yabloko party chairman Nikolai Rybakov. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova The liberal Yabloko party filed an appeal with Russia’s Supreme Court on Friday, challenging a ruling to cancel the registration of the party’s federal slate of candidates for next month’s State Duma elections. The Supreme Court accepted the appeal and scheduled a hearing for Monday, Aug. 17, at 10 a.m. Moscow time. “We’ll prove that the truth is on our side and on the side of the people who support us,” Yabloko chairman Nikolai Rybakov told reporters outside the courthouse after he and his party submitted the appeal. Last week, the Supreme Court disqualified Yabloko from parliamentary elections in September for copyright violations during campaign activity and for breaking campaign finance laws by allegedly accepting funding from abroad. That ruling removes Russia’s oldest liberal party — and what was the only registered party campaigning on a pro-peace platform — from the nationwide party-list ballot. title: Zabaikalsky Region Declares State of Emergency Following Summer Flooding
text: Zabaikalsky Region Declares State of Emergency Following Summer Flooding Aug. 14, 2026 Flooding in Chita, the capital of Zabaikalsky. @shcheglovais / MAХ Authorities in Far East Russia’s Zabaikalsky region declared a state of emergency on Thursday following a summer of torrential rainfall and three consecutive flood waves. Governor Alexander Osipov said Friday that the emergency declaration was needed in order to speed up financial aid to residents impacted by the flooding and repairs to damaged infrastructure. Rainfall across the region — located along the Chinese border roughly 4,700 kilometers (2,900 miles) east of Moscow — reached up to 250% of seasonal averages this summer. Emergency officials issued five separate storm warnings as three distinct flood waves battered nine municipal districts. “It’s been a tough summer,” Osipov wrote in a post on Telegram. title: Russia Dismisses Calls for Black Sea Ceasefire
text: Russia Dismisses Calls for Black Sea Ceasefire By Reuters Aug. 14, 2026 A cargo vessel leaves a port in Odesa. REUTERS / Nina Liashonok Russia's Foreign Ministry on Friday dismissed the idea of a ceasefire with Ukraine in the Black Sea, saying it saw no grounds for "half-measures" that would offer a respite to Ukrainian forces. Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks against commercial ships in the Black Sea in recent weeks, which has driven world grain prices higher. In a statement, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine of "brazen acts of terrorism" against shipping while making no mention of Russia 's own attacks. "We view these attacks as a deliberate policy aimed at destabilizing civilian shipping in the Black Sea region, to escalate tensions further and prolong the conflict, all with the blatant acquiescence of regional neighbors," Zakharova said. title: State Prosecutors Seek 12-Year Prison Sentence for Lev Shlosberg
text: State Prosecutors Seek 12-Year Prison Sentence for Lev Shlosberg Aug. 14, 2026 Lev Shlosberg in court. yabloko.ru State prosecutors in the northwestern city of Pskov have asked a judge to sentence veteran opposition politician Lev Shlosberg to 12 years and one month in prison for “discrediting” and spreading “fake news” about the Russian military , the liberal Yabloko party said Friday. The requested sentence combines maximum penalties under wartime censorship laws with a previous November 2025 conviction in which Shlosberg was sentenced to 420 hours of community service for violating Russia's “ foreign agent ” law, the exiled news outlet Mediazona reported . Shlosberg, a senior member of Yabloko, pleaded not guilty, instead accusing prosecutors of “discrediting” Russian law. The military “ fakes ” charge stems from a Feb. 25, 2022, Telegram post in which Shlosberg reshared content from the now-defunct Ekho Moskvy radio station. The post featured a British tabloid cover depicting President Vladimir Putin alongside a bloodied woman. title: Moscow Court Jails Man 23 Years for Spying for Poland
text: Moscow Court Jails Man 23 Years for Spying for Poland Aug. 14, 2026 Georgy Pirogov in court. FSB A judge in Moscow has sentenced a Russian man to 23 years in prison after finding him guilty of treason for allegedly spying for Poland, Russia’s FSB security service said Friday. Georgy Pirogov was handed the sentence along with a fine of 800,000 rubles ($9,500). The FSB’s statement, which was shared by state media outlets, came more than a month after the exiled news outlet Mediazona, citing an anonymous source, first reported the verdict in mid-July. According to independent media reports , Pirogov relocated to Georgia following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine to work as an industrial climber. He vanished in July 2024 during a business trip to Uzbekistan and resurfaced days later inside Moscow’s Matrosskaya Tishina pre-trial detention facility. Neither Russian nor Uzbek authorities have explained how Pirogov was detained or transferred across international borders. FSB video shared by the state-run news agency TASS on Friday showed Pirogov’s interrogation, during which he admitted to working with Polish intelligence. title: Fire Breaks Out at Ust-Luga Port After Ukrainian Drone Attack
text: Fire Breaks Out at Ust-Luga Port After Ukrainian Drone Attack Aug. 14, 2026 The Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga. Krasny (CC BY-SA 4.0) A fire broke out Friday at Russia’s Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga, a major hub for oil exports, following a Ukrainian drone attack on Friday, regional authorities said . Leningrad region Governor Alexander Drozdenko said firefighters managed to put out the blaze at Ust-Luga later in the morning and that no one was hurt in the attack. He offered no details on the extent of the damage at the facility. Earlier, Drozdenko said air defenses shot down more than 50 drones overnight across the Leningrad region surrounding St. Petersburg. In a separate overnight incident, the governor of the neighboring Tver region said drone debris damaged an outer wall at a warehouse belonging to major online retailer Wildberries. No injuries were reported at the site, which marks the latest in a series of strikes on commercial logistics hubs. Authorities in the Belgorod region, which borders Ukraine, said later on Friday morning that a person riding a bike was struck and killed by a drone.
